name: IEC Schmitt-trigger inverter (rectangular form)
summary: IEC inverter with the hysteresis mark, used to clean up slow edges while inverting the signal.
description: This element combines the 1 qualifier, the hysteresis mark and output negation. It inverts the signal while switching at two thresholds, which makes it a common choice for debouncing contacts with an RC network and for building simple relaxation oscillators.

When a Schmitt inverter forms part of an oscillator or delay with external resistors and capacitors, the drawing should keep those components next to the element and note the intended timing. The symbol alone gives no clue that it is part of a timing circuit.
Thresholds, hysteresis width and supply range are device data. Different logic families have markedly different thresholds even though the symbol is identical.
readingNotes: Check for external RC parts that turn the inverter into a timing circuit.
Confirm the output negation as well as the hysteresis mark.
drawingChecklist: Show both the hysteresis mark and the output negation.
Note the intended timing if used as an oscillator or debounce.
distinction: The Schmitt buffer has the same hysteresis mark but no output negation.
